brief: Bring mobile up to parity with web: buying requests entry point, image moderation wiring, swipe-back gesture on both platforms, liquid-glass tab bar, saved listings/searches account bug, VIN reveal click-gate. Local changes only, no EAS push until told.

goals.title: Buying requests
goals.objective: Investigate why Buying Requests isn't reachable in mobile UI despite screens existing, wire up entry points
goals.evidence: Backend confirmed working (curl /api/buying-requests returns 200, valid JSON). All screens (BuyingRequestsScreen, BuyingRequestDetailScreen, PostBuyingRequestScreen) already existed and were wired into AppNavigator, reachable via a small 'Wanted' pill in Explore's category row - not broken, just far less discoverable than web's prominent top-level nav item + dedicated 'Post a Buying Request' link (confirmed via frontend/src/components/Header.js). Added a distinct 'Looking to buy instead?' card below the category grid in PostListingScreen.js's category-choice screen (the natural place a user posting anything would look), navigating to PostBuyingRequest. Verified: eslint clean on PostListingScreen.js.

goals.title: Image moderation
goals.objective: Investigate whether imageModeration.js (nsfwjs/blazeface) is actually wired into the upload flow in PostListingScreen, wire it up if not
goals.evidence: Image moderation (imageModeration.js, nsfwjs+blazeface for nudity/face detection) was already fully wired into PostListingScreen.js's single shared pickImages/ImageCropperModal flow, applied uniformly to all 4 categories (car/bike/plate/parts) - confirmed via grep showing all 4 ImageSection instances share the same onPickImages callback and single ImageCropperModal instance. Real bug found: ImageCropperModal's 'Use Photo' button only awaited image compression, not the parent's onConfirm (which runs moderation) - spinner disappeared and modal looked idle while moderation silently ran in the background, explaining why the feature seemed invisible/absent to the user, plus a latent double-tap race risk. Fixed by threading a moderating prop into ImageCropperModal, ORed with its own processing state for the button's busy/spinner condition, plus a 'Checking photo...' title swap for clarity. Verified: eslint clean on both files, npx expo export bundled successfully (important given imageModeration's tfjs-react-native dependency chain caused real bundling failures earlier this session).

goals.title: Swipe-back gesture
goals.objective: Enable iOS-style swipe-to-go-back on both iOS and Android stack navigators
goals.evidence: Added gestureEnabled: true + gestureDirection: 'horizontal' to the shared screenOptions object used by all 5 stack navigators (Auth/Explore/Post/Saved/Profile) in AppNavigator.js. react-native-screens ~4.16.0 and @react-navigation/native-stack ^7.3.16 (both current versions) support this cross-platform - iOS already defaults to it, Android needed it explicit. eslint clean.

goals.title: Liquid glass tab bar
goals.objective: Research and implement native blur/liquid-glass style bottom tab bar for iOS with Android equivalent
goals.evidence: No literal 'Liquid Glass' API exists in Expo SDK 54/React Navigation - implemented the real, standard, cross-platform equivalent: expo-blur's BlurView (already installed, ~15.0.8) as tabBarBackground with tabBarStyle position:absolute + transparent background in AppNavigator.js's MainTabs, working on both iOS and Android via expo-blur's native implementations. Proactively fixed a foreseeable regression: making the tab bar float/absolute meant its 3 main tab screens (Explore, Saved, Profile) would have their last content items hidden behind it, since existing bottom padding (40px/48px, or none on ProfileScreen) was less than the bar's ~76px+ footprint. Added TAB_BAR_CLEARANCE=100 constant to theme.js and applied it to all 3 screens. eslint clean (only pre-existing unrelated apostrophe warning), npx expo export bundled successfully.

goals.title: Saved listings/searches bug
goals.objective: Diagnose why account isn't reading saved listings/saved searches correctly, check if saved searches exists at all on mobile, fix end to end
goals.evidence: Two distinct things found and fixed: (1) CRITICAL auth bug - apiClient.js's getBestAccessToken() only ever read AsyncStorage's 'auth_data' key (authService's own email/password token store). Google/OAuth sign-in only creates a Supabase session and never writes to that key, and setAuthHeader (confirmed earlier this session as a genuine no-op via git blame) was supposed to bridge the two but never did anything - meaning every apiClient call for Google-signed-in users (saved listings, saved searches, everything requiring auth) went out with zero Authorization header, silently. This is the real 'not reading the account properly' bug. Fixed by adding a Supabase-session fallback in getBestAccessToken(). (2) Saved searches didn't exist on mobile at all (confirmed via grep - zero hits vs multiple web files). Backend already has full CRUD (GET/POST/DELETE /api/user/saved-searches, confirmed live via curl). Implemented end to end: 'Save this search' button in ExploreScreen (gated by useAuthPrompt, matching existing app patterns) posting category/query/filters/result_count; a new 'Searches' tab in SavedScreen with fetch/list/delete; tap-to-reapply that navigates back to Explore and re-populates activeTab/search/category-specific filters via route params. Verified: eslint clean (only pre-existing unrelated warnings), npx expo export bundled successfully including the new apiClient<->supabaseClient cross-import (checked for circular-import risk beforehand, confirmed none).

goals.title: VIN reveal click-gate
goals.objective: Add the extra tap-to-reveal step for already-eligible users, matching web, for admin tracking purposes
goals.evidence: Added vinVisible state and handleVinReveal to CarDetailScreen.js, replacing the auto-show-on-eligible behavior with a real click-gate matching web exactly: every tap fires trackLeadEvent('car', car.id, 'vin_open') regardless of eligibility; only eligible users (isOwner || phone_verified) additionally get setVinVisible(true) + a vin_reveal event on that same tap. Non-eligible users still get the phone-verification prompt as before.
